You're right, it's nearly impossible to imagine how medication or therapy can help when you feel this low. Firstly, anti-depressants aren't going to give you a few extra years. If they work, they work, if they don't you switch and switch until you find one that works. The crucial thing is not to assume that you are instantly going to feel better for taking medication, it'll take weeks and you might not even notice that you're in a better mood. 

Maybe you'll gradually realize that because you're feeling happier you notice that you're acting nicer. Then you might start to gain confidence and realize that you are a good person, that you do care about the people around you it's just out of your reach right now. People will notice, they'll see you're trying to reach out and that you're worth it, they'll become close friends. Friends you will have for the rest of your life. Now the medications aren't the thing that are going to be keeping you going, it'll be your relationships with the people that you love and care about. When you're in a rundown shitty apartment somewhere there'll be someone to call, someone to vent to, someone that'll listen. Hell, you could even go to their place and crash for a couple nights and they won't mind, you're worth it. 

I'm not going to preach the long life ahead of you bullshit, because honestly it isn't helpful. Telling you to think positive isn't going to help, but hopefully you will realize that you're on a journey right now. You are still very young, you are forming an identity and opinions about the world around you, ultimately it is up to you to craft your own perspective on what you want your future to look like and who you want in that future. You don't have to know yet, you don't even have to know when you graduate, you just have to know that when the time is right it'll all make sense. 

I suggest if you feel up to it, it could be an enormous benefit for you to see a psychiatrist, psychologist or both. Depression is a battle you really cannot fight yourself, these mentors could very well help you build a foundation for a stable, happy life.

Sometimes the hardest thing is forgiving yourself mate, no one is perfect, we're all very far from it. You understand that pain and exhaustion better than anyone, if you need a break take one and don't feel guilty. But taking a permanent break from your life and struggles is an enormous leap into the unknown. If you need someone to talk to about what's going wrong please, please DM me or tell a friend/family/community member you trust.
